title: Cloze Test
intro: A cloze test is a short passage with several blanks; for each blank you choose the best of four words. It combines vocabulary, grammar and a feel for how the passage flows. The key is to read the whole passage first for its overall sense, then fill each blank so it fits both the grammar of the sentence and the meaning of the paragraph.

items.name: Read the whole passage first
items.formula: sense and direction guide every blank

topics.name: Vocabulary Gaps
topics.details: Some blanks need the word whose meaning fits the passage. Use the surrounding sentence for tone and look for collocations — words that naturally pair.

solved.problem: She had to ___ a difficult decision.
He paid careful ___ to the lecture.

topics.name: Grammar Gaps
topics.details: Some blanks need the grammatically correct form — the right tense, article, preposition, or part of speech. Use the rest of the sentence to decide.

solved.problem: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel. (rains/rained)

topics.name: Connectors & Flow
topics.details: Many blanks are connectors that signal the logical relationship between ideas. Read what comes before and after the blank to pick the right one.

solved.problem: He was tired, ___ he kept working. (but/so)
It rained, ___ the match was cancelled. (so/but)
___ he is rich, he is humble. (Although/Because)

unsolved.problem: He ran fast ___ missed the bus. (but/so)
___ it was cold, he went out. (Although/So)

topics.name: Contextual Choice
topics.details: When two options are both grammatically fine, the passage's overall meaning decides. Track the theme and the writer's stance across sentences.

solved.problem: How do you choose between two grammatically valid options?
solved.solution: By the passage's overall meaning and tone.

solved.problem: A passage praising a scheme needs fillers of which tone?
What final check confirms a cloze answer?
solved.solution: Re-read the sentence in the flow of the paragraph.

solved.problem: Why read the whole passage before filling blanks?

unsolved.problem: Borderline blanks are decided by the passage's ___.
After filling, re-read the sentence in the ___.
Reading the full passage first reveals its ___.
The best filler does not ___ with earlier sentences.

shortcuts: Read the whole passage first — direction and tone guide every blank.
Each blank must fit BOTH grammar and meaning.
Connectors: match the logic (but=contrast, so=result, because=cause).
Use collocations (make a decision, pay attention, take a risk).
For ties, let the passage's overall tone decide; re-read in flow.
mistakes: Filling blanks one by one without reading the whole passage.
Choosing a grammatically right word that clashes with the meaning.
Using the wrong connector for the logical relationship.
Ignoring collocations and picking a loose synonym.
pyq: SSC sets a short cloze passage with five blanks mixing vocabulary, grammar and connectors. Reading the whole passage first and matching both grammar and sense is the reliable approach.

flashcards.q: Read what first in a cloze?
Each blank must fit grammar and ___?

summary: A cloze test blends vocabulary, grammar and flow. Read the whole passage first, then fill each blank so it satisfies the grammar of the sentence and the meaning/tone of the paragraph. Match connectors to the logical relationship, lean on collocations, and re-read in context to confirm.
